title: Insertions making a search tree unbalanced
summary: Repeatedly inserting nodes on the same side lengthens one branch level by level until an initially balanced binary tree violates the balance condition.
context: A node's balance factor is its left subtree height minus its right subtree height, with leaf height 0 and empty subtree height −1; a tree is balanced only when every node's balance factor has absolute value at most 1. The balance factors below are computed from the connections shown.

This example is an ordinary binary search tree without rotational rebalancing. The three subfigures have 3, 4, and 5 nodes in order and are labeled "Perfect binary tree", "Balanced binary tree", and "Ordinary binary tree"; the right child of root 4 remains leaf node 5 throughout.
result: A tree can lose its perfect shape and still be balanced. An AVL tree restores balance through rotations after insertions.

frames.title: Insertions making a search tree unbalanced
frames.explanation: Initially, root 4 has left and right children 3 and 5. When 2 is inserted, 2 is less than both 4 and 3 and attaches to the left of 3; although the bottom level is no longer full, both 4 and 3 have balance factor 1, so the tree stays balanced. When 1 is inserted next along 4 → 3 → 2 to the left of 2, the balance factors of 3 and 4 both become 2, making the tree unbalanced.

steps.title: Initial perfect binary tree
steps.explanation: Initially, root 4 has leaf children 3 on the left and 5 on the right, with 3 nodes filling two levels; every node has balance factor 0, so the tree is both perfect and balanced.
steps.key_state: Initial root 4 connects to left 3 and right 5; all 3 nodes have balance factor 0.
steps.announcement: Show the initial perfect binary tree with root 4 and left and right children 3 and 5.

steps.title: Still balanced after inserting 2
steps.explanation: Insert 2: being less than 4 and 3, it becomes the left child of 3. Root 4 now connects to left 3 and right 5, 3 connects only to left 2, and 2 and 5 are leaf nodes, for 4 nodes in total. Both 4 and 3 have balance factor 1, so the tree is no longer perfect but remains balanced.
steps.key_state: After inserting 2, root 4 connects to left 3 and right 5, and 3 connects to left 2; 4 and 3 both have balance factor 1, still balanced.
steps.announcement: Insert 2 to the left of 3; the tree is no longer perfect, but 4 and 3 both have balance factor 1 and remain balanced.

steps.title: Unbalanced after inserting 1
steps.explanation: Insert 1: search leftward along 4→3→2 and attach 1 to the left of 2. The left chain is now 4→3→2→1, and root 4 also has right leaf node 5, for 5 nodes in total. Node 3 has left height 1 and right height −1, while root 4 has left height 2 and right height 0, giving both a balance factor of 2 and making the tree unbalanced.
steps.key_state: After inserting 1, the left chain is 4→3→2→1 and root 4 connects to right leaf 5; both 3 and 4 have balance factor 2.
steps.announcement: Insert 1 to the left of 2; the balance factors of node 3 and root 4 both become 2.
